sents.t: Now it is October, and Oakville looks different.
The leaves on the trees on Maple Street are red, orange, and yellow.
Now I understand the name of my street!
On Monday, it was warm and sunny.
On Tuesday, it was cold and windy.
On Wednesday morning, it was only forty degrees!
I didn’t have a warm coat, so I bought a jacket, a scarf, and gloves.
On Saturday, Carlos drove Emma and me to an apple farm outside town.
We picked apples and drank hot apple cider.
I also chose a big orange pumpkin for my apartment.
In the evening, I raked the leaves in front of our building with Rosa.
Max jumped into the big pile of leaves again and again.
My mother called me on Sunday.
“Is it cold in America?” she asked.
“But autumn here is beautiful. Americans call it ’fall,’ because the leaves fall from the trees.”

comp.q: What color are the leaves on Maple Street?
How cold was it on Wednesday morning?

o: because people fall in the leaves
